transcript.content: Hello, thank you for coming in. Can you tell me what’s been troubling you or what brings you here today?

Hi, thank you so much for seeing me. I really appreciate it. Um, I hope I'm starting in the right place, but... I guess I've just been having a little bit of trouble with my communication lately? It's probably just stress, honestly, I don't want to make a huge deal out of it. 

But when I'm writing my artist statements, or doing client notes, or even just talking in meetings... my words have started kind of jumping around. Like, I'll go from talking about the physical textures of a piece, straight into the financial budgets, and then into... um, like, secret meanings behind things. And people keep telling me they can’t really follow what I’m trying to explain. It's a little embarrassing, to be honest, because I really want to be professional. 

Does that make sense? I want to make sure I'm giving you the right kind of information.
Can you tell me more about how your thoughts and words are jumping around? Does it feel like your mind is racing, or are you having trouble keeping your thoughts in order?

Um, yes, I think racing is probably a good word for it, though I really hope it doesn't sound too... erratic? It's just that my thoughts can move so fast sometimes. Like, I'll be working, and suddenly images for a new piece, titles, the language for a grant proposal, the colors I need to mix, and a conversation I had yesterday—they all just kind of stack on top of each other. 

It happens before I can even finish focusing on one single idea. I try really hard to keep it all organized, I promise I do, but it just gets a little overwhelming sometimes. Am I explaining that okay? I just want to make sure I'm giving you a clear picture without sounding too scattered.
Have you ever experienced any unusual perceptions, like hearing voices that others don’t hear or believing things that other people might not believe to be true?

Um... well... I guess I have noticed a couple of little things, but honestly, it's probably just my imagination working overtime. Being in the studio alone all day can play tricks on you, right? I'm sure it's completely normal for creative types. 

But, um, sometimes when I'm working by myself, I'll hear... like, a woman's voice? Just really quietly, commenting on things, and it sounds like it's coming from right behind my supply shelves. And sometimes I'll smell this really sharp scent of hot metal near a piece I haven't finished yet. 

It feels so real in the moment, it really does, but then I'll go look and... obviously, there's nobody there, and nothing is burning. It's just my brain being a little overactive, I think. I really hope that doesn't make me sound crazy or anything. Is that the kind of thing you were asking about? I want to make sure I'm answering your question right.

Have you ever experienced a time when your mood was unusually high, irritable, or you felt extremely energetic for several days or more—where you felt like you didn’t need much sleep, were doing or saying a lot more than usual, or your ideas were racing in a different way than what you're describing now?

Um... yes, I think I have had times like that. I really hope it doesn't make me sound difficult to work with, because I try so hard to be a good collaborator. But... sometimes, for a few days or maybe a week, I'll get into this state where I just feel so lit up? Like I'm almost unstoppable, and every single idea I have is just brilliant and needs to happen right away. I get so much done during those times, which is great for my career, right? 

But... the downside is, if someone questions an idea, or if a collaborator makes even a small comment... I can get really irritable. Like, I might snap at them in a way that is just... a lot bigger than the situation actually calls for. I always feel terrible about it afterward, I really do. I don't want to be that kind of person. 

Does that sound like what you're asking about? I just want to make sure I'm giving you the right examples without making myself sound too awful.

Have you ever had a period of time when you felt down or hopeless almost every day, lost interest in things you usually enjoy, or had significant changes in your sleep or appetite that lasted for at least two weeks?

Um, no... I don't think I've ever really had anything quite like that. I mean, I guess everyone gets a little sad or frustrated sometimes, especially if a project isn't coming together right? But I've never felt completely hopeless, or... or lost interest in my art or the things I love. 

I try really, really hard to keep a positive outlook on things, I promise I do. I'm a pretty optimistic person usually! And my appetite and sleep are mostly fine, well, except for when I'm in one of those really energetic phases I just mentioned. But otherwise, no, I don't think I've ever been down for two weeks straight like you're describing. 

I hope that's a good thing? Like, I just want to make sure I'm understanding your question right and giving you accurate information... but it's definitely a good thing that I don't get that way, right?
Have you noticed any recent changes in your sleep patterns or energy levels that have lasted for more than a few days, even outside of your creative periods?

Um... well... I guess my sleep has been a little bit different lately, but I honestly think it's just because I've been so focused on my work. It's not a bad thing, I promise! 

Lately, if I work really late into the night, I've noticed I can just sleep for maybe two or three hours... and then I wake up feeling just completely bright and ready to keep going. I'm not tired at all the way I normally would be if I only got a few hours. It actually feels really nice to have all that extra time to get things done, you know? 

I know you're supposed to get eight hours and everything, and I usually try to be really good about taking care of myself. But right now, my body just doesn't seem to need it as much. That's okay, isn't it? As long as I'm feeling energized and getting my work done, it's probably fine, right? I just want to make sure I'm giving you the right details without making it sound like I'm neglecting my health.
Have there been times when your elevated mood or high energy led to problems in your relationships, work, or other important areas of your life?

Um... oh, I really hate to admit this, because I pride myself on being a good professional. I try so hard to be reliable and keep everything running smoothly, I promise I do. 

But... yes, I guess there have been a few hiccups. Just some minor things, mostly! Well... maybe not completely minor. I have missed a couple of paid deadlines recently, which I feel absolutely terrible about. And sometimes in meetings, I think I end up confusing my collaborators. I just get so excited and have so many ideas at once, and I guess it can be hard for them to follow me. 

The hardest part was... they actually had to postpone one of my upcoming exhibitions. They told me that my notes and the proposals I was sending them just... stopped making enough sense for them to use. I felt so embarrassed when they said that. I really didn't mean to cause any trouble for anyone. 

I'm working really hard to get better at organizing my thoughts so it doesn't happen again. That's the kind of thing you were asking about, right? I really hope that doesn't make me sound completely irresponsible... I really am trying my best.
